description: Master per-character record: display names, group classifications, ordered variation list and the IDs that join to every other character subsystem table (animation, effect, sound, UI, battle parameters, capture, arcade, etc.), plus a few direct gameplay scalars.

ID.simple: Character ID (CP_xxx / CN_xxx) used as the row key and across the game.
ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). DTM_FindCharacterRow / GameCharacter_FindVariationRow style lookups resolve every other table's character ID back here; AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows stores the matching row pointer as CharacterRow (+0x3A0). Values such as CP_000 and CP_010 also appear as the first/last entries of other tables. The row key is not read as a value by most consumers, which instead use their own slot ID.

Id_GlossaryText_Name.simple: GameText ID of the character's normal display name.
Id_GlossaryText_Name.technical: FName text key (e.g. GLS_NAME_CP_010) passed to IGameWidgetTextSettingInterface::SetTextIdOnly or GameTextManager::GetText/GetGameTextById across select, lobby, shop, customize, ranking and story UI. The customize character view keeps a TMap<CharacterId, NameTextId> from Row->Id to this value. No per-row localization is stored here; the text manager resolves the current language.

Id_GlossaryText_StoryName.simple: GameText ID of the name used in story/battle-talk contexts.
Id_GlossaryText_StoryName.technical: FName text key, row +0x18. Used by the battle-talk widget and the story character-select widget to set the speaker/character name text separately from the standard display name.

Id_Character_Transformation.simple: Character ID of this character's transformed/alternate battle form.
Id_Character_Transformation.technical: FName; None means no transformation. Battle setup appends an extra default entry for the transformed character (with the same variation index) to the preload/walk list, battle preload resolves its rows, level sequencer substitutes the ID for transformation sequences, and the sequence-name builder appends the transformed ID to sequence names. A finder with bCheckNone=true avoids matching None.

CharacterGroup.technical: EGameCharacterGroup (uint8: None, JujutsuSorcerers, CursedSpirits, CurseUsers, CursedWombDeathPaintings, CursedObjects, Invalid). Cast to uint8 and passed to AGameManager::OnBattleWon on battle victory; also gates character-specific action-controller behavior (CN_240), command-list contents and the text ID returned by Story_GetUniqueWordsTextId. Default construction sets None.

CharacterPairGroup.simple: Pair/team compatibility group for paired character sequences.
CharacterPairGroup.technical: EGameCharacterPairGroup (uint8: None, JujutsuSorcerers, CursedSpirits, CursedWombDeathPaintings, Independent, Invalid). GameSequencerManager checks that a team of at least two characters all share a non-Independent group before selecting the paired 'APPEARANCE_02' voice path. Default construction sets None.

Id_CharacterVariation.simple: Ordered list of costume/variation row IDs, indexed by the character's variation index.
Id_CharacterVariation.technical: TArray<FName>, row +0x30. ResolveDataRows resolves Id_CharacterVariation[InVariationIndex] without a bounds check during battle setup; the same indexed access drives character capture, preload, material controller, item ownership/thumbnail checks, result screens, visual lobby and sequencer. Many UI paths do bounds-check and fall back to element 0 or NAME_None; some (e.g. customize costume view) index unguarded. None entries are used as empty costume slots, and availability is checked via the variation's Id_Item.

Id_CharacterAnimationSet.simple: CharacterAnimationSetDataTable row that owns the character's animation montage list.
Id_CharacterAnimationSet.technical: FName joined to CharacterAnimationSetDataTables (DTM +0x4B0). Battle preload and level sequencer resolve it; the animation set's Id_CharacterAnimation entries are expanded into montage FileName lists. Mission-character overrides can replace it through StudioBattleCharacterOverrides::AnimationSetIdOverride (GamePvESettings copies the character value as the default), so this field is the default rather than an unconditional choice.

Id_CharacterTrap.simple: List of CharacterTrapDataTable rows whose trap actor Blueprints this character uses.
Id_CharacterTrap.technical: TArray<FName>, joined to CharacterTrapDataTables (DTM +0x4C0). BattleAssets_Traps_12BCE80 iterates the array, skips None, resolves each CharacterTrap row and appends its FileName_BP into the battle preload list. The same set is used by other battle setup paths via the trap table.

Id_CharacterEffect.simple: CharacterEffectDataTable row for this character's visual effects.
Id_CharacterEffect.technical: FName joined to CharacterEffectDataTables (DTM +0x4D0). ResolveDataRows resolves it into AGameCharacter::EffectRow (+0x3C8), which status/aura/blow code reads for colors, effect IDs and effect transforms. Battle preload also expands it into a FileName_BP asset list. None skips preload; a missing row leaves the cached pointer null (GameCharacter uses an optional finder).

Id_CharacterShikigami.simple: List of CharacterShikigamiDataTable sets that enumerate this character's shikigami.
Id_CharacterShikigami.technical: TArray<FName> of set IDs (DTM +0x4F0). BattleAssets_Shikigami_12BD9B0 walks each set's Id_Shikigami, resolves Shikigami rows (DTM +0x6C0) and adds their FileName_BP plus all referenced ShikigamiAnimation FileName values to preload lists; BattleBase/LevelSequencer also resolve the sets for shikigami spawning in battles/cutscenes.

Id_CharacterDecal.simple: CharacterDecalDataTable row listing this character's decal actor Blueprints.
Id_CharacterDecal.technical: FName joined to CharacterDecalDataTables (DTM +0x500). None skips the lookup; otherwise the row's FileName_BP array is appended to the battle preload asset list. Only characters with decals have a non-None value in the export.

Id_CharacterUnique.simple: List of CharacterUniqueDataTable rows holding this character's unique numeric parameters.
Id_CharacterUnique.technical: TArray<FName> indexed as a list (not by variation). ResolveDataRows reserves one pointer per entry and fills AGameCharacter::UniqueRows (+0x420) with optional lookups into CharacterUniqueDataTables (DTM +0x570), keeping null for missing rows; later character-specific code indexes UniqueRows by the same order.

DamageRate_AutoCombo.simple: Character-specific damage multiplier for auto/curse-powered combos.
DamageRate_AutoCombo.technical: float, constructor default 0.0. AGameCharacter::GetAutoComboDamageRate returns CharacterRow->DamageRate_AutoCombo * Rates.Scale4C; that accessor is used by character-specific action controllers, cursed-energy actions, shikigami actions and traps to compute action damage rate. Zero therefore means no contribution rather than a neutral multiplier of 1.

LinkComboCursedEnergyExpRate.simple: Per-character multiplier on cursed-energy experience gained from link combos.
LinkComboCursedEnergyExpRate.technical: float, default 0.0 (row +0x8C). The status controller computes a truncated global gain (Global::LinkCombo_CursedEnergyExp_Add * 0.01 * level difference), applies buff/equipment/binding-vow modifiers, then multiplies by this field before adding to the character's cursed-energy gauge.

AutoAttackDash_NextActionType.simple: Action requested after an auto-attack dash connects/closes distance.
AutoAttackDash_NextActionType.technical: EGameCharacterActionType, default None (row +0x90). FGameCharacterAction's auto-attack logic calls AddRequest with this value when the target is close enough on the ground plane and vertically overlapped; UGameCharacterActionController::GetAutoAttackDashNextActionType returns the same field. Exported values are concrete normal-air attack types.

AutoAttackDash_Distance.simple: Distance threshold for auto-attack dash and its air warp (centimetres).
AutoAttackDash_Distance.technical: float, default 0.0 (row +0x94). Auto-attack dash returns when 2D target distance is at least this value; AutoAttackDashAirBegin warps to the secondary target with TargetDistance = 0 when closer than the threshold, else the threshold itself. Also checked by the air-dash warp short-stop logic; used as a world-space distance with Unreal centimetre units.

Id_Action.simple: ActionDataTable row that defines the character's action set.
Id_Action.technical: FName joined to ActionDataTables. ResolveDataRows resolves it with GameCharacter_Override(Overrides.ActionIdOverride, Row->Id_Action), so mission-character overrides can replace it; Setup copies the character value into StudioBattleCharacterOverrides::ActionIdOverride by default. Command-list UI also resolves the same row for display.

Id_CommandList.simple: CommandListDataTable row used to display the character's move list.
Id_CommandList.technical: FName; None short-circuits the command-list widget (no command list row is fetched). Otherwise FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_CommandList> over CommandListDataTables. Several exported characters have None here.

ActionControllerType.simple: Selects the character's action-controller and bone-controller implementations.
ActionControllerType.technical: EGameCharacterActionControllerType, default None. AGameCharacter::CreateActionController(Setup.ControlType85, Row->ActionControllerType) and CreateBoneController(Row->ActionControllerType, yaw, pitch, FootIKLimit) both use it; the setup's ControlType85 (from mission character) is passed separately to the action controller factory. Default construction sets None.

AIType.simple: AI brain/type discriminator for this character.
AIType.technical: EGameCharacterAIType, default None (row +0xA9). CreateBrain receives static_cast<uint8>(CharacterRow->AIType) unless an explicit override byte (0xFF means use the row) is supplied; UGameCharacterBrain_AI::BrainCreate95 jumps over AIType values 1..46 to build per-character AI behavior.

AutoAimLimitAngleYaw.simple: Maximum yaw angle (degrees) applied by auto-aim.
AutoAimLimitAngleYaw.technical: float, default 0.0 (row +0xAC). Copied through CreateBoneController into the bone-controller setup; GameCharacterBoneController clamps the computed auto-aim yaw to [0, limit] and applies the sign from the cross product. Zero means no auto-aim yaw.

AutoAimLimitAnglePitch.simple: Maximum pitch angle (degrees) applied by auto-aim.
AutoAimLimitAnglePitch.technical: float, default 0.0 (row +0xB0). Passed with yaw into CreateBoneController; the bone controller clamps computed pitch to [0, limit] with a sign from target height, and later animation updates clamp AutoAimPitch to [-limit, +limit].

SituationAttackVoicePlayDistance.simple: Distance within which a situation-attack voice line is allowed to play.
SituationAttackVoicePlayDistance.technical: float, default 0.0 (row +0xB4). GameCharacterActionController compares the world-space distance between the owner and its secondary target against this value before enabling the situation attack voice.

PvEAllyWeights.simple: Relative weight for selecting this character as a random PvE ally.
PvEAllyWeights.technical: float, default 0.0. GamePvE_PickAllyCharacter_1305990 starts from the selectable character rows, drops the kept character and any row with weight <= 0, then performs a weighted random pick using this value. It does not affect story-defined allies or PvP selection.

StoryCharaGraphPlacementIndex.simple: Sort order for this character's icon on the story character graph.
StoryCharaGraphPlacementIndex.technical: int32, default 0. GameStoryCharaGraphWidget sorts icon widgets with RowA->StoryCharaGraphPlacementIndex < RowB->StoryCharaGraphPlacementIndex; lower indices appear first.

Id_CharacterBaseParameter.simple: CharacterBaseParameterDataTable row with base combat stats.
Id_CharacterBaseParameter.technical: FName joined to CharacterBaseParameterDataTables (DTM +0x3F0). ResolveDataRows resolves it into BaseParameterRow, applying Overrides.BaseParameterIdOverride when present; PvE/command-list/VS-enemy widgets read the same row directly for display and growth. GamePvESettings copies the value as the default override.

Id_CharacterCursedEnergy.simple: CharacterCursedEnergyDataTable row defining cursed-energy gauge behavior.
Id_CharacterCursedEnergy.technical: FName joined to CharacterCursedEnergyDataTables. ResolveDataRows resolves it into CursedEnergyRow with Overrides.CursedEnergyIdOverride; command-list/interval widgets and GamePvESettings also read/copy it.

Id_CharacterSelect.simple: CharacterSelectDataTable row controlling select-screen placement and availability.
Id_CharacterSelect.technical: FName (row +0xD0); None removes the character from selectable lists (MainMenuCollection, Ranking, customize chat, item-ownership filters). ResolveDataRows caches the resolved row as SelectRow (+0x3C0); the select widget sorts by PlacementIndex and the visual lobby by VisualLobbyPlacementIndex. Items with CharacterSelect=None are treated as non-playable/non-selectable in several UI paths.

Id_CharacterCamera.simple: CharacterCameraDataTable row for lock-on camera gaze height.
Id_CharacterCamera.technical: FName (row +0xD8). UGameCharacterVirtualCamera::OnTargetChanged uses the locked-on target's value to find the row and set LockOnGazeHeight (fallback 135.0 without a row); see CharacterCameraDataTable documentation.

Id_CharacterUI.simple: CharacterUIDataTable row controlling battle HUD/gauge behavior.
Id_CharacterUI.technical: FName (row +0xE0). Resolved by Status_FindCharacterUIRow across many battle and growth widgets: button guide, damage combo, target cursor (height rate), battle character data (gauge type), command list, VS-enemy growth widgets. Battle-demo setup removes characters with a None value from its random pool.

Id_CharacterSpecialAttack.simple: CharacterSpecialAttackDataTable row defining the character's special moves/domain expansion.
Id_CharacterSpecialAttack.technical: FName (row +0xE8). ResolveDataRows resolves it into SpecialAttackRow with Overrides.SpecialAttackIdOverride; battle preload uses the row's Id_DomainExpansion to preload domain assets, and GamePvESettings copies the value into the override struct by default.

Id_CharacterOperation.technical: FName joined to CharacterOperationDataTables; ResolveDataRows stores the result as OperationRow (+0x3DC) and fails character setup when the row cannot be found.

Id_CharacterChat.simple: CharacterChatDataTable row supplying symbol-chat text and voice IDs.
Id_CharacterChat.technical: FName (row +0xF8). ResolveDataRows caches it as ChatRow (+0x3E0); chat message/result/customize widgets also look it up directly. None or a missing row leaves no chat messages for that character.

Id_SituationOverview.simple: SituationOverviewDataTable row defining this character's overview poses.
Id_SituationOverview.technical: FName (row +0x100) joined to SituationOverviewDataTables. It is resolved in customize character/pose/card widgets, user-customize info and all pose-driven character-capture paths; the overview row's Id_SituationOverviewPose[...] selects a pose which in turn supplies ally/enemy animations and weapon IDs for captures.

Id_CharacterCapture.simple: CharacterCaptureSetDataTable row identifying this character's UI capture configurations.
Id_CharacterCapture.technical: FName (row +0x108). FindCharacterCaptureRow stops entirely when None, otherwise resolves the CharacterCaptureSet row and picks a CharacterCapture row by requested capture type; used for all scene-capture loading/spawning/montage selection. See CharacterCaptureSetDataTable documentation.

Id_CharacterArcade.simple: CharacterArcadeDataTable row for this character's Arcade mission setup.
Id_CharacterArcade.technical: FName (row +0x110). CharacterArcade's Id_MissionCharacter selects the player's mission-character settings in GamePhase_BattleArcade; its Id_ArcadeMissionSet and ClearFlagConditions drive the Arcade root-select widget. None means the character has no Arcade root data.

FootIKLimit.simple: Per-character foot-IK reach/limit values passed to bone controllers.
FootIKLimit.technical: TArray<double> (row +0x118), copied into AGameCharacter's bone-controller setup by CreateBoneController(..., Row->FootIKLimit). Base InitFootIK101 uses element [0] as the Limit for left/right ankle IK; character-specific controllers index additional elements (e.g. CN_140 uses [1] for other limbs). Some controllers/shikigami use the same array type. No default values are set in the row constructor; exported rows commonly start with 10-30 and trailing zeros.

CullingBoundingBoxScale.simple: Scale applied to the character's mesh bounds for camera-inside/culling tests.
CullingBoundingBoxScale.technical: FVector (row +0x128) returned by AGameCharacter::GetCullingBoundingBoxScale (interface slot 90); null row returns ones. GameCharacterManager multiplies MeshBounds.BoxExtent component-wise by this scale when testing whether the camera lies inside the character's bounding box, affecting placement/culling decisions. Exported values include 0.75 and 1.0 per axis.

OverrideJustGuard_HitSlow_Attacker.simple: Optional hit-slow (time dilation) rate applied to the attacker on a just-guard.
OverrideJustGuard_HitSlow_Attacker.technical: float, constructor default 0.0, exposed through AGameCharacter::GetOverrideJustGuardHitSlowAttacker (interface default -1). In GameBattleDamage a negative value falls back to Global::JustGuard_HitSlow_Attacker; otherwise this value is passed to TimeManager::RequestTimeDilation as the slowdown rate for non-projectile just-guards. Zero would therefore override the global rate with zero, not fall back.

OverrideJustGuard_HitSlow_Time_Attacker.simple: Optional duration of the attacker's just-guard hit-slow.
OverrideJustGuard_HitSlow_Time_Attacker.technical: float, constructor default 0.0, exposed through AGameCharacter::GetOverrideJustGuardHitSlowTimeAttacker (interface default -1). GameBattleDamage uses it in place of Global::JustGuard_HitSlow_Time_Attacker when non-negative when requesting attacker time dilation; only applies to non-projectile damage and is paired with the rate override above.

Id_Item.simple: Item ID representing ownership/unlock of the base character.
Id_Item.technical: FName (row +0x148), e.g. ITM_CHARACTER_CP_121_00. GameCharacter_GetSelectableRows removes rows that have a CharacterSelect ID but whose Id_Item is neither None nor in stock/unlocked (GameItem_HasStock). This is the character-level gate distinct from the per-costume Id_Item on CharacterVariation rows.

notes: Export contains 48 Character rows; each row carries the full cross-table ID set, and many IDs are None for characters that lack a given subsystem (e.g. no select row, no command list, no shikigami).

Character rows are the central join: game code resolves them by character ID (DTM_FindCharacterRow, DTM +0x3E0), then fans out to CharacterBaseParameter (+0x3F0), CharacterVariation (+0x400), CharacterCursedEnergy (+0x410), CharacterSpecialAttack (+0x420), CharacterCaptureSet (+0x430), CharacterCapture (+0x440), CharacterSelect (+0x450), CharacterCamera (+0x460), CharacterUI (+0x470), CharacterImage (via variation), CharacterMaterial, CharacterAnimationSet (+0x4B0), CharacterTrap (+0x4C0), CharacterEffect (+0x4D0), CharacterWeapon (+0x4E0), CharacterShikigami (+0x4F0), CharacterDecal (+0x500), CharacterChat (+0x550), CharacterUnique (+0x570), CharacterArcade (+0x5A0).

StudioBattleCharacterOverrides can replace BaseParameter, CursedEnergy, SpecialAttack, Action and AnimationSet IDs; GamePvESettings seeds those overrides from the Character row, so the row values are defaults in battle/mission contexts.
Row constructor defaults: enum fields None, all scalar rates/angles/distances 0.0, StoryCharaGraphPlacementIndex 0; pointer/array fields are left empty by default.
There are no per-locale CharacterDataTable variants in the export; localized names are referenced via Id_GlossaryText_* text IDs.

Evidence is reconstructed C++ with cited retail RVAs; some consumers index arrays without bounds checks, which is a retail behavior, not a documentation blank. No claim is made about byte-identical matching, Blueprint-only uses or retail rows absent from the partial Content export.

usages.detail: ResolveDataRows resolves all mandatory linked rows and caches CharacterRow, sub-rows and optional arrays.
BattleAssets_FindCharacter and the collectors expand traps, effects, shikigami, decals and images into preload lists.
Battle preload indexes Id_CharacterVariation and resolves animation sets, effects and other assets.
Capture loading starts from Character::Id_CharacterCapture and Id_CharacterVariation.
Select widget resolves CharacterSelect rows and sorts by placement index.
Just-guard hit-slow overrides are read from the attacking character's row.
PvE ally lottery weights characters by PvEAllyWeights.
